About us

Impact

In 2024, NP4SE member governments began contributing membership dues. In a landscape of competing priorities and limited budgets, our member countries chosing to dedicate national resources to NP4SE is the clearest evidence of the network’s high utility and long-term relevance to national development.

Spotlights

Guyana

Guyana – Getting Ready for First Oil

The Challenge
In 2019, with "First Oil" fast approaching, Guyana faced the daunting task of regulating a world-class petroleum sector using outdated 1986 laws that did not sufficiently protect the State’s interests. The government needed to rapidly bridge gaps across capacity, institutional, and legislative frameworks before production started.
The Intervention
NP4SE (as NPG) facilitated a critical inter-agency workshop, which also included existing technical assistance providers. The workshop focused on dismantling information asymmetries—such as the fact that the revenue authority lacked access to the joint operating agreements necessary for cost audits.
The Impact
This session resulted in a comprehensive "Landscape Map of Immediate Actions," which clearly defined the technical, financial, and environmental tasks required of every government agency. By identifying support resources like the NPG Helpdesk and peer-to-peer exchanges with Ghana and Uganda, Guyana was able to enter its production phase with a coordinated roadmap for cost recovery, crude valuation, and environmental stewardship.
SurinameSomalia

Breaking the Policy Silos

The Problem
Governments often operate in silos. For example, before our training & workshops on Aligning Goals, officials from Suriname and Somalia identified "limited coordination" and a lack of "awareness/alignment" between leading institutions as a primary barrier to a realistic national strategy.
The Outcome after our intervention
  • 100% Coordination breakthrough: Every participant surveyed reported that the course helped them identify new, specific points for inter-agency coordination within their government.
  • Understanding of the intersection of petroleum, national development goals, and NDCs shifted from a baseline of "Some" to "High" or "Very High".
  • Participants gave a nearly perfect score when asked if the learning would directly impact their work performance, indicating a high level of practical utility.
Uganda

Uganda – Turning Climate Law into Action

The Challenge
While Uganda passed the National Climate Change Act in 2021, the technical ministries lacked the specific ‘checklists’ needed to monitor and enforce emissions limits in the petroleum sector.
The Intervention
Through a series of Emissions Training & Workshops (2022–2024), NP4SE brought together Energy and Environment officials to co-design regulatory tools.
The Impact
The Ugandan delegation successfully developed a Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) framework specifically for oil and gas. They are now implementing emissions monitoring checklists that allow the government to hold operators accountable to national climate goals.
Suriname

Suriname – Asserting its Carbon-Negative Status

The Challenge
Suriname, a carbon-negative nation, faces the complex task of developing significant offshore oil discoveries without compromising its global environmental leadership.
The Intervention
In 2023 NP4SE provided a strategic White Paper and technical briefings to the Surinamese government, outlining how new producers can aim for the lowest sector emissions while investing in carbon negative projects that support national development goals.
The Impact
At COP28, President Chan Santokhi utilized NP4SE’s research to declare a clear national mandate: “Suriname will maintain its carbon negative status even when the offshore oil and gas industry is developed.” This demonstrated how the network equips heads of state with the technical confidence to navigate global climate politics.
Ghana

Ghana – "Just-In-Time" Negotiation Support

The Challenge
Government regulators often face highly experienced International Oil Companies (IOCs) with far greater resources during contract negotiations.
The Intervention
In November 2025, NP4SE held a specialized Licensing Strategy and Negotiation Workshop for government officials.
The Impact
Participants from the regulatory agency and the national oil company reported that the training was applied immediately to a live negotiation with an IOC. By providing specific fiscal benchmarks and negotiation tactics exactly when they were needed, NP4SE helped shift the balance of power back to the state.
Feedback
"The course was timely and has provided me with tools to enhance my negotiating task."
All member countries

The Shift to Member Ownership

The Challenge
International networks often struggle with long-term sustainability and staying relevant to the changing needs of the Global South.
The Action
Recognizing the unique value of the peer-to-peer space, NP4SE members voted to contribute membership dues in 2024, leaving the contribution voluntary for countries without commercial discoveries.
The Impact
This shift has created a sustainable governance model that is independent of external donor shifts. It ensures that NP4SE remains producer-led, answering only to the governments that fund and lead it. This financial commitment is a global rarity and a testament to the trust placed in the network.
